class.name: SteamAudioProbeVolume
class.brief_description: Volume used to generate Steam Audio probes and bake pathing and reflections.
class.description: Place this node so its [member size] box covers the listener area. Generate probes, then bake pathing and/or listener-centric convolution reflections. At runtime the batch is loaded into [SteamAudioServer]. The properties in the Bake group configure pathing only, while Reflection Bake properties configure baked reverb. Changing either group does not modify existing baked data; run the corresponding bake again to apply new settings. Generation and baking use a snapshot of [SteamAudioGeometry] nodes in the edited scene; [SteamAudioDynamicGeometry] is not included. Uniform Floor generation and pathing bakes add a thin fallback floor at the bottom of this volume. Only one Steam Audio bake can run in the process at a time. Older batches without stored probe positions and radii must be explicitly regenerated before baking. The Steam Audio SDK cannot read these spheres back from a loaded batch; current volume settings are not used to guess them. Removing the node from the tree cancels and discards its pending bake, waiting for the SDK worker to stop.

method.name: generate_probes
method.description: Generate probes in this volume (centroid or uniform-floor) and store them in [member baked_data]. Does not bake pathing. In the editor, also writes [member baked_data] to [member save_path].

method.name: bake_pathing
method.description: Bake pathing (probe-to-probe visibility) into [member baked_data]. Calls [method generate_probes] first if there is no batch yet. In the editor this runs in the background (see [method cancel_bake]); at runtime it blocks until finished.

method.name: bake_reflections
method.description: Bake listener-centric convolution reverb at every probe. Players with [member SteamAudioPlayer.reflection] enabled automatically use available baked data and fall back to real-time reflections outside a usable probe neighborhood. In the editor this runs in the background.

method.name: cancel_bake
method.description: Request cancellation of an editor pathing or reflection bake. Reflection cancellation is cooperative and delivered at an SDK progress callback. Pathing finishes in the background and discards its result; native pathing cancellation is not used. [method is_baking] remains true until the worker exits and cleanup finishes; cancelled results are not applied or saved. Removing the node or closing the scene may wait for this worker.

method.name: save_baked_data
method.description: Write [member baked_data] to [member save_path] as its own resource file. If [member save_path] is empty, a path is chosen next to the scene, or under [code]res://steam_audio_bakes/[/code] if the scene has not been saved yet.

method.name: get_probe_count
method.description: Number of probes in [member baked_data], or 0 if none.

method.name: get_probe_positions
method.description: World-space probe positions used for viewport gizmos.

method.name: is_baking
method.description: True while a bake is running or awaiting finalization, including cancellation and resource-change callbacks. Becomes false before [signal bake_finished] is emitted.

method.name: is_baking_reflections
method.description: True when the active editor bake is a reflection bake.

method.name: get_bake_progress
method.description: Bake progress from 0 to 1 while [method is_baking] is true.

members.member: Radius in meters of the sphere around each probe used for path-visibility sampling. A larger radius samples more possible positions around probes and can preserve connections near obstacles, but may accept paths through wider openings than a point-sized probe would.

Number of sample points placed within each probe's [member bake_radius] when testing visibility between two probes. Each probe pair traces this value squared rays. Higher values make visibility tests more robust but can greatly increase pathing bake time.
Number of CPU worker threads used by the pathing baker. Higher values may reduce bake time while increasing CPU usage. This does not affect runtime pathing cost.

Minimum fraction of unoccluded visibility rays required to connect two probes. Higher values reject partially blocked connections and produce more conservative paths. Steam Audio requires the visible fraction to be strictly greater than this value, so [code]1.0[/code] rejects every connection.

Serialized probe batch, including pathing data after a bake. Stored as an external resource at [member save_path]. Reassignment is rejected while [method is_baking] is true. A bake snapshots its input metadata; direct edits to resource properties during a successful bake are replaced by the completed result.

Standalone .res or .tres file to write [member baked_data] to, not an embedded resource path containing [code]::[/code]. Filled automatically after the first successful save if empty. A failed save leaves the resource's path binding unchanged. New automatic paths distinguish the scene and node names and skip existing files and directories. Explicit paths and existing standalone resource paths retain their binding and are overwritten on save.
Centroid places one probe at the volume center. Uniform Floor places probes on a grid above solid geometry.

World-axis-aligned size of the generation volume, in meters, centered on this node and multiplied by its global scale. Rotation does not rotate the generation region. Generated probe positions stay fixed in world space until regenerated.
Horizontal spacing between uniform-floor probes, in meters.
Height above the floor for uniform-floor probes, in meters.
Maximum allowed path length between probes, in meters. Increasing it lets sound propagate over longer routes, at the cost of increased pathing bake time and baked-data memory.
Maximum number of times each ray reflects from geometry. Higher values capture longer, more accurate reverb tails at increased bake time.
Number of directions considered when generating diffusely reflected rays. Higher values can slightly improve diffuse-reflection accuracy at increased bake time.
Minimum source-to-surface distance in meters used when calculating reflected energy. Sources closer to a surface are treated as being this far away, preventing unrealistically large energy values.
Ambisonic order of the baked impulse responses. Higher orders retain more directional detail but increase bake time, baked-data size, and runtime memory and processing cost.
Number of rays traced from each probe. Higher values reduce simulation noise and improve accuracy at increased bake time.

Length in seconds of each impulse response stored in the bake. Longer durations preserve longer reverb tails but increase disk size, load time, runtime memory, and convolution cost. Values above [member reflection_simulated_duration] are clamped to the simulated duration.

Length in seconds simulated when generating each impulse response. Longer durations model larger spaces and longer tails but increase temporary memory use and bake time. This may exceed [member reflection_saved_duration] so the saved bake retains only the early response.
Number of CPU worker threads used by the reflection baker. Higher values may reduce bake time while increasing CPU usage. This does not affect runtime reflection threads.
Maximum distance in meters at which two probes can receive a direct visibility connection in the baked pathing graph. Increasing it can produce simpler routes, but increases pathing bake time.

signal.name: bake_started
signal.description: Emitted when an editor pathing or reflection bake begins.

signal.name: bake_finished
signal.description: Emitted after an editor pathing or reflection bake completes, is cancelled, or fails, and its job resources have been released. Not emitted when a pending bake is discarded because the node leaves the tree.

constants.constant: One probe at the center of the volume.
Grid of probes a fixed height above floors.
